verdict.rationale: A runtime probe records the published phaser npm package (4.2.1) as MIT-licensed, and Phaser's source is hosted in the public phaserjs/phaser GitHub repository. Together these mean a user can read the product's source under an open license. missing for 10: a first-party documentation statement of the license and open-source status (the MIT finding comes only from npm metadata via a probe), and an explicit LICENSE file citation from the GitHub repo.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
